message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most famous American composers—spanning classical, film, Broadway, and popular music—whose work has had a lasting impact both in the United States and worldwide:

| Composer | Years | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|-------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* (opera) | Blended jazz idioms with classical forms; helped legitimize jazz as a serious art form. |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man*, *Elmer Gantry* (film score) | Known as “the father of American classical music”; his lush orchestration captured the American spirit. |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | *West Side Story* (musical), *Candide*, *On the Waterfront* (film score) | A conductor, composer, and educator who bridged Broadway, symphonic, and popular music. |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Scores for *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park*, *Harry Potter* (early films) | One of the most recognizable film composers; his themes have become cultural touchstones. |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*, *The Hours* (film score) | Pioneer of minimalism; his repetitive structures influence contemporary classical and popular music. |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains*, *The Desert Music* | Another minimalist icon; his use of phasing and tape loops reshaped modern composition. |
| **Stephen Foster** (1826–1864) | “Oh! Susanna”, “Camptown Races”, “Beautiful Dreamer” | Often called the “father of American songwriting”; his songs are staples of early American folk music. |
| **Irving Berlin** (1888–1989) | “God Bless America”, “White Christmas”, “Blue Skies” | Prolific songwriter whose tunes became standards in American popular culture. |
| **Charles Ives** (1874–1954) | *The Unanswered Question*, *The Swimmer*, *Concord Hymn* | Early modernist who incorporated American vernacular music into classical forms. |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine*, *The Death of Klinghoffer* | Contemporary composer known for his postminimalist style and politically engaged works. |

These composers represent a broad spectrum of American musical history—from the early 19th‑century folk traditions to the cutting‑edge minimalism of the late 20th century—and each has left an indelible mark on the cultural landscape.

We might mention classical composers like George Gershwin, Aaron Copland, Leonard Bernstein, John Williams, etc. Also mention contemporary composers like Philip Glass, Steve Reich, etc. Also mention folk and popular composers like Stephen Foster, Irving Berlin, etc. But the question likely expects classical composers.
